purpose: Fresh validation and controlled CPU timing of cached exact objective-guided pruning.
primary_quality: Exact same final mask, greedy deletion path and angles on all128 held-out groups; independently recompute original and cached statevector distributions and metrics. Any mismatch is a failure, not evidence of statistical equivalence.
primary_cost: First32 freshly generated groups fixed in advance; five repetitions per method with randomized interleaved method order, one BLAS thread, one warmup on a training input. Report per-case medians, paired bootstrap ratio of means and median ratios. No competing research experiment is run during this benchmark.
timing_scope: Selector only on the same precomputed public h,J; includes cache construction and near-tie checks, excludes shared LLL/Babai/encoding, angle training, statevector evaluation and circuit compilation. Cheap controls batch50 calls per repetition to improve timer resolution and amortize instrumentation.
training: No new training: same residual global angles frozen in EXP017, loaded through EXP021 frozen models. Implementation developed using64 old examples and mathematical correctness tests only.
limitations: Implementation acceleration of the existing p=1 algorithm, not a new pruning rule or novelty claim.
Analytic expectation call count need not decrease; speed comes from caching and vectorization.
Single CPU environment and tiny same-distribution16-qubit examples; no scaling or end-to-end quantum advantage.
Ideal probabilities only; no noise simulation, cloud calls or QPU usage.
